The room §5I’m§0 in has no light source, and neither does the hallway. 

It’s like the world here naturally emits just enough light to be able to see the outlines of things, and not any actual finer details.

Nevermind the light. §5I

stride down the hall, §5my§0 shoes clacking loudly against the wood floor. 

No matter how delicate §5I§0 place §5my§0 foot, if the impact doesn’t make any noise, the boards themselves sure do.

Great. 

If anything is in here

with §5me§0, it sure as shit knows that §5I’m§0 here. 

§5I§0 turn to the first door on the left. 

The knob is broken off, making opening it that way impossible. 

§5I§0 briefly consider opening it how §5I§0 intended on opening the first door, but

decide against it when the smell hits §5me§0. 

An overpowering stench assaults §5me§0 from under the door. 

A stink like rotten bodies and ancient mold makes §5me§0 recoil. 

§5I§0 couldn't imagine what's behind it, but §5I§0 have no interest in

finding out. 

With §5my§0 interest in opening the first door destroyed, §5I§0 turn to look at the second door. 

I tread down the hall, and look at the staircase as §5I§0 pass by it. 

It rounds the

corner and goes down a second flight. 

§5I§0 can't see whatever is on the floor below. 

The second door actually has a knob on it, unlike the first one.

The condition of the door and its knob is rough, with a thick

layer of rust on its handle and the hinges that hold it to the wall. 
Grabbing it and twisting it has it yield for §5me§0 with little effort. 

Weirdly, it's 
completely silent. 

No creak, no moan or groan from such a

dilapidated door. 

What's even weirder than the lack of noise is what sits behind it. 

No, worse than weird. At the center of this room is a gravestone. 

The sight immediately makes §5me§0 feel confused and uncomfortable.

What is it doing here? 

How could it even possibly be here? 

The stairs to the right in the hallway showed that this place has different floors. 

That would mean someone somehow brought a thousand pound slab of rock

up §5who§0 knows how many stairs. 

§5I§0 don't want to go anywhere near it, but §5I§0 feel compelled to do so. 

Something is mandating, requiring, demanding, begging that §5I§0 get closer to it.

§5I§0 have to investigate.

So §5I§0 do. 

§5I§0 enter the room slowly and cautiously, checking the sides as §5I§0 pass through the doorway. 

Despite the low light, or perhaps because of it rather, §5I§0 don't see anything else.

Just this massive slab

of stone in the middle 
of the room. 

§5I§0 run §5my§0 right hand along the surface of the stone. 

§5My§0 left hand still hums with the pain of §5my§0 earlier meltdown. 

The stone is cold to the touch. Ice cold.

It feels like a 
block of ice. 

But the surface is so smooth, machine perfect in its finish.

The light is too low to make out what color it is, but even if it was, §5I§0 couldn't guess what kind of stone it is.

Tombstones are

usually made of granite or something, right? 

There doesn't 
seem to be anything on the front side of the stone. 

If there is, it's too dark to perceive it. 

But there does seem to be something on the

back side. 

Chiselled into the back side of the tombstone is some writing. 

§5I§0 can't read what it says, and feeling it out doesn't really work out how §5I§0 want it to.

Whatever is written here, §5I§0 am completely

unable to make it out. 

§5Who§0's grave is this? 

The idea of someone being mourned in this way makes §5me§0 upset. 

Do §5I§0 have people §5who§0 would mourn §5me§0? 

Is there anyone §5who§0 knows §5my§0 name?

§1Oliver§0 does. 
He knows §5me§0, 
and §5I§0 know him. 

§5I§0 knew of him, but 
now §5I§0 know §5who§0 he is. 

§5I§0 wish §5I§0 could find him. 

§5I§0 wonder if he's seen §5my§0 message to him.

A feeling of deep unease washes over

§5me§0, threatening to drown §5me§0. 

§5I§0 don't want to be anywhere near this thing anymore. 

§5My§0 curiosity 
has been sated. 

§5I§0 need to leave. 

§5I§0 turn to face where the door is, and move

towards it. 

The doorway is still where §5I§0 expected it, but there's another door next to it. 

Facing in the direction that would lead it towards that sealed off, foul smelling room. 
Unlike the door in the hallway, this door has

its knob. 

It should open extremely easily, so long as the lock permits §5me§0 to. 

But do §5I§0 want to? 

§5My§0 curiosity is strong, but §5my§0 intuition screams not to. 

§5I§0 am in a room with

a gravestone, and the room next to this smells of death. 

It doesn't take much to make §5my§0 mind wander. 

§5I§0 shake §5my§0 head, bringing §5myself§0 back to reality. 
No. 

§5I§0 don't want anything

to do with whatever's behind that door. 

§5I§0 head towards the still open door, and re-enter the hallway. 

To §5my§0 left is the only other door in this hallway, and ahead and just to the right is the stairs.

Something about

those stairs makes §5me§0 feel so uneasy. 

§5I§0 don't know why, but §5I§0 dread having to go down them. 

§5I§0 turn to face 
the last door 
to §5my§0 left. 

It sits in a similar state of disrepair as the other three

doors. 

Seeing how bad 
the wood is 
discolored and 
the hinges have rusted has made 
§5me§0 realize how 
much more clearly 
§5I§0 can see now. 

§5My§0 eyes must be adjusting to the light.
